title: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs staff protest over welfare and leadership
location: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs headquarters, Abuja
scope: One staff gathering at ministry headquarters; later staff session is a response, not a separate protest.
organizer: Federal Ministry employees; the later report identifies a union chair, but the protest organizer is not specified.

state_target.evidence: Protest was at federal ministry and called for minister redeployment and action on staff grievances.

demands_original: Request for minister redeployment; working tools, staff welfare, training, inclusion, and workplace concerns.
participants_original: No attendance estimate reported; staff workforce does not establish gathering size.

start_date.summary: The Sep12 Guardian follow-up says workers protested two days earlier, establishing Sep10.

end_date.summary: Sources describe the Sep10 action; they do not establish that street protest continued after that day.

location.summary: Both reports place it at the Ministry of Women Affairs headquarters in Abuja.

scope.summary: One workplace gathering; the later staff discussion is response context, not another episode.

organizer.summary: Reports identify ministry employees and, in the later session, a union chair. Formal protest organizers are not named.

state_target.summary: Action was directed at a federal ministry and minister.

demands.summary: Staff sought the minister’s redeployment and raised welfare, work-tool, training and inclusion complaints.

participants_original.summary: Neither report gives a turnout estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No simultaneous attendance count; workforce size is not turnout.

state_response.summary: The minister acknowledged complaints and engaged staff in a later session; dialogue was reported, but implementation is not established.

open_questions: Did at least 50 people assemble simultaneously?
Who organized the Sep10 protest beyond the ministry staff?
Did any demands receive implementation or only dialogue?

title: Residents block Makurdi–Lafia highway and demand government action after killings
location: Makurdi–Lafia Federal Highway near Guma/Makurdi LGAs, Benue State
scope: One local community gathering following attacks; no linked multi-location campaign reported.
organizer: Residents of communities along the highway; organizer not identified.

state_target.target: Benue State governor and authorities responsible for security.
state_target.evidence: Residents demanded government action to end attacks and insisted the governor address them.

demands_original: Demand for government action to end attacks following the killings of five people.
participants_original: Article reports a road blockade and use of three victims’ bodies; it gives no participant count.
threshold_50_evidence: No count or estimate establishes 50 simultaneous participants.

start_date.summary: Channels dates the road protest to Sep20 after killings Friday and early Saturday.

end_date.summary: The article reports the blockade on Sep20; no end time or later action is described.

location.summary: Makurdi–Lafia Federal Highway near Guma and Makurdi LGAs, Benue State.

scope.summary: One road blockade by local residents; no national or multi-city organization.

organizer.summary: Residents are described collectively; no formal organizer is named.

state_target.summary: Protesters demanded government action and insisted the Benue governor address them.

demands.summary: Action to end attacks after deaths of residents/farmers.

state_response.summary: Security agencies sought to restore passage; no response to the demand is documented.

open_questions: Did at least 50 people participate simultaneously?
Was the governor or another state official engaged with the demand?
How long did the blockade last?

title: Indigenous contractors block Finance Ministry gate over unpaid federal contract debts
location: Federal Ministry of Finance entrance, Abuja

state_target.target: Federal Ministry of Finance and Federal Government as contracting authority.
state_target.evidence: Contractors demanded immediate payment of federal debts for completed projects.

demands_original: Payment of funds owed for completed federal projects.
participants_original: No attendance count; association membership or contract amounts are not turnout.

start_date.summary: Channels reports the action on Wednesday Sep3.

end_date.summary: Article reports the action on Sep3; duration is not stated.

location.summary: Gate of the Federal Ministry of Finance in Abuja.

scope.summary: One ministry-gate action, with no other sites reported.

organizer.summary: Indigenous Contractors Association of Nigeria is identified.

state_target.summary: The complaint concerns nonpayment for federal contracts and was directed at the federal ministry.

demands.summary: Placards demanded payment of debt for completed projects.

state_response.summary: Minister entered through another gate; a permanent secretary approached the protesters but was rejected. No resolution is reported.

open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend simultaneously?
Did the permanent secretary’s approach lead to any meeting or decision?

title: PENGASSAN members blockade petroleum regulators’ offices in Abuja during refinery dispute
location: NNPCL, NMDPRA and NUPRC premises, Abuja; counts by office unknown.
scope: PENGASSAN’s national industrial-action directive accompanied reported blockades at three offices; no per-site counts or simultaneity detail.
organizer: Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (PENGASSAN), under a national executive directive.

state_target.target: The sites are state petroleum bodies, but the stated grievance is dismissal by a private refinery and government-directed demand is not explicit.
state_target.evidence: Union alleges labor-law/constitutional violations but principally protests Dangote Refinery’s dismissal of unionized workers.

demands_original: Opposition to alleged dismissal of unionized refinery workers; citations to labor law, Constitution and ILO conventions.
participants_original: No attendance count at any site; a nationwide service withdrawal is not gathering attendance.
threshold_50_evidence: No individual site count establishes the 50-person threshold.

start_date.summary: Channels reports the blockades on Monday Sep29.

end_date.summary: No end date or duration is reported.

location.summary: NNPCL, NMDPRA and NUPRC offices in Abuja; crowd counts by site absent.

scope.summary: Nationally directed action, but actual presence and headcount at each listed site are unknown.

organizer.summary: PENGASSAN and its national executive directive are identified.

state_target.summary: The public sites are state bodies and the union cites law, but no specific request for government action is reported; the main dispute is with Dangote Refinery.

demands.summary: Protest against alleged dismissal of workers for unionizing.

participants_original.summary: No count at any office or national aggregate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Do not infer attendance from workforce or nationwide work stoppage, offices, or number dismissed.

state_response.summary: The report quotes the company’s justification of layoffs; it does not document government response to the blockades.

open_questions: Does this qualify as a public state-directed protest or remain a private-company labor dispute?
Did any individual office have at least 50 simultaneous attendees?
Were the three reported blockades concurrent and organized as one action?

title: Retired soldiers protest at Finance Ministry over unpaid entitlements
location: Federal Ministry of Finance headquarters, Abuja
scope: A week-long protest is reported as suspended on Sep8; exact onset date and month ownership are unresolved.
organizer: Retired soldiers led by retired Sergeant Ekundayo Alisame.

state_target.target: Federal Government, Ministry of Finance, Military Pension Board and military authorities.
state_target.evidence: Retirees sought payment and recalculation of benefits/allowances and appealed to the president/military authorities.

demands_original: Payment of outstanding entitlements and a transparent calculation framework.
threshold_50_evidence: No simultaneous attendance estimate; threshold unresolved.

start_date.summary: BusinessDay calls it week-long and says it began the previous week, but provides no exact onset; whether it began in late August or September remains unknown.

end_date.summary: BusinessDay reports the canopy dismantled and protest suspended Monday Sep8.

location.summary: Federal Ministry of Finance headquarters in Abuja.

scope.summary: One week-long Finance Ministry protest; no other location reported.

organizer.summary: Retired Sergeant Ekundayo Alisame is identified as the protest leader.

state_target.summary: Protest was at the Finance Ministry; the leader appealed to President Tinubu and military authorities.

demands.summary: Benefit calculation, payment arrears and allowances.

state_response.summary: Finance, military pension and related officials met the protest leader; government promised payments for that week. Implementation is unknown.

open_questions: Did the protest begin in August or September?
Did at least 50 people gather at any point?
